teaching.task: Explain dynamic equilibrium using equal non-zero forward and reverse rates, stable composition and a stated closed-system model. Distinguish equal rates from equal concentrations and steady observation from evidence of exchange.
teaching.causalExplanation: In the supplied one-to-one model, forward conversion removes A at the rate reverse conversion replaces it. Both rates are non-zero, but their effects cancel, keeping each concentration steady. Concentration is amount per volume, not traffic per time.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Connected Australian English with sealed-drink context and traffic metaphor. Essential visual relationships are spoken. No viewing-command sequence, promised marks or unverified historical anecdote. Gentler 130 WPM planning allowance is a hypothesis, not selected delivery.
teaching.openingDecision: Rhetorical surprise: can an unchanged drink still exchange CO₂? It motivates the observable/process distinction. Actual independent response is protected later in quick-check.
teaching.understandingCheck: Synthetic C ⇌ D transfer with unequal steady concentrations and supplied equal non-zero conversion counts. Require classification, causal balance and why steady readings alone would be insufficient. Prompt/feedback are separate planned recordings with assembled silence, not a narration tag.
